verdict.rationale: PayPal has a general-purpose webhook system that supports subscribing to event types (with retries and signature verification) over HTTPS, and the REST API surface includes orders/subscriptions that could emit lifecycle events; the agent toolkit also exposes order/refund/dispute tools. However, there is no documented mapping showing that agentic-commerce-specific order lifecycle events (created/updated/fulfilled/canceled for AI-agent-initiated orders/carts) are pushed via webhooks — the cart API (createcart/getcart) is polling-based, not event-push, and Store Sync says the order simply lands in the existing OMS rather than emitting agent-specific lifecycle webhooks. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that agentic/cart orders trigger the general webhook event types, a list of agent-specific lifecycle event names, and confirmation that fulfillment/cancellation of AI-agent orders is webhook-pushed rather than requiring polling via getcart.
